_README: This file is the entire Knowledge Hub. resources.html reads it at load and
builds every card, count, filter and search result from it. There is no CMS
and no backend — to publish, add an entry below and push.
EVERY COUNT ON THE PAGE IS COMPUTED FROM THIS ARRAY. Nothing is hardcoded.
An empty array renders honest empty states, not fake numbers. Do not add
placeholder resources to make the page look fuller — that is the same
false-advertising problem flagged on the landing page.
REQUIRED per entry: id, title, summary, category, format, level,
language, published, url.
OPTIONAL: author, minutes, featured, thumb, topics[].
level    must be one of the ids in `levels` below (beginner | expert).
language must be one of the ids in `languages` below (en | es | fr |
pt | de). Category, format, level and language are four INDEPENDENT
axes — a visitor can narrow by all four at once. Do not add levels or
languages to `categories`; the sidebar renders each axis separately.
category must be one of the ids in `categories` below. A resource that
belongs in two places may instead use `categories`: ["ppc","inventory"] —
it then appears under, and counts toward, every category listed.
format   must be one of the ids in `formats` below.
published is ISO yyyy-mm-dd. Sorting is newest first.
featured: true promotes it to the 'Featured' block. The newest featured
entry becomes the large card; the next two fill the stack beside it.
url may be a relative path to a page in this repo, or an external link.

resources.title: Why Amazon Sellers Overestimate TAM (And Why Smaller Markets Often Build Bigger Businesses)
resources.summary: Market size tells you how much money exists, not how much remains available. Sellers quote TAM because it's the biggest number, but businesses survive inside what they can realistically win and hold.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Your Next Product Should Make Your Existing Business Stronger
resources.summary: Six unconnected products share nothing; six connected ones share fifteen advantages. The best launches don't just add revenue — they lower acquisition costs, deepen suppliers and make everything already built perform better.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Every Product Is a Capital Allocation Decision
resources.summary: $2M of revenue on $1.8M of capital is a worse business than $800K on $180K. Most sellers ask whether a product can make money; the best ask whether it deserves capital that can only be spent once.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The Best Products Usually Don't Look Exciting
resources.summary: Excitement is public, so it attracts competition. Boring markets stay boring — and predictable demand, repeat purchasing and reliable forecasting are what actually compound into a business.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The Hidden Cost of Complexity in Product Portfolios
resources.summary: Another SKU almost always adds revenue. Whether it adds value is a different question — every SKU is thirteen ongoing obligations, and a $40K product takes the same meeting slot as a $2M one.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The Opportunity Cost of Every Product Launch
resources.summary: The biggest cost of a launch isn't manufacturing, advertising or inventory — it's everything else the same capital could have done. A profitable decision is not necessarily a good one.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Stop Looking for Winning Products. Start Looking for Winning Markets.
resources.summary: Products have life cycles; markets have ecosystems. The mistake isn't picking the wrong product — it's picking the right one in a market you'll never own. Knowledge compounds inside markets, not SKUs.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Why Most Product Research Is Looking at the Wrong Data
resources.summary: Search volume, revenue estimates and review counts all describe demand that already happened. Research isn't about finding good ideas — it's deciding which single opportunity deserves capital you can only spend once.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Every Business Eventually Becomes the Sum of Its Decisions
resources.summary: Revenue, products and markets are temporary. Companies form like sediment — one ordinary layer at a time — and organisations, unlike people, remember every decision. Improving one means negotiating with choices made years ago.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The CEO's Job Changes Every Year. Most Founders Never Notice.
resources.summary: The skills that built the business are often the ones stopping it growing. Three versions of the founder — doing, coordinating, running out of hours — and the promotion after CEO that almost nobody takes.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Most Dashboards Don't Help You Make Better Decisions. They Help You Feel Better About Bad Ones.
resources.summary: Sellers have more data than ever and many decide worse. Dashboards were built to display information, not to help anyone act — and a screen of red alerts every morning quietly trains an organisation to be reactive.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The Only Sustainable Competitive Advantage Isn't Your Product. It's Your Decision-Making Speed.
resources.summary: Products, suppliers, costs and software all get copied eventually — most advantages have an expiry date. An organisation that decides and learns faster than its competitors doesn't, because every decision is also a chance to learn.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Your Most Valuable Asset Isn't Inventory. It's Attention.
resources.summary: Capital can be borrowed, inventory manufactured, staff hired. Attention can only be redirected — and in most growing businesses it, not money, is the binding constraint. What leaks it, and what systems are really for.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Growth Is Usually a Cash Flow Problem Disguised as a Sales Problem
resources.summary: Past a certain size, demand stops being the constraint and capital becomes it. Why every sale creates nine future obligations, why profit can't pay a supplier deposit, and why allocation — not budgeting — is the CEO's real job.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Your Business Is Producing Exactly What It Was Designed to Produce
resources.summary: If the same mistakes keep returning, your systems are producing them as designed. Why replacing people rarely changes results, why symptoms surface far from their cause, and what to ask instead of who is to blame.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Your Business Isn't Growing. It's Becoming More Complex.
resources.summary: Growth is linear. Complexity is exponential. Ten products aren't ten times harder — they're forty-five relationships. The challenge after your first million isn't more customers, it's stopping complexity from outrunning your systems.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: You Don't Have a Sales Problem. You Have a Decision Quality Problem.
resources.summary: The gap between a $500,000 business and a $50 million one isn't better products, advertising or people. It's thousands of marginally better decisions, compounding — and most problems are the delayed result of a decision made months earlier.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The Amazon PPC Flywheel: Why the Best Campaigns Become Better Over Time
resources.summary: Most sellers treat advertising like electricity — on, sales rise; off, sales stop. The best treat it as a flywheel, where every campaign leaves behind reviews, ranking, relevance and data that make the next one cheaper.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The Most Expensive PPC Mistake Isn't Spending Too Much. It's Stopping Too Soon.
resources.summary: Most sellers kill winning campaigns before they become great — confusing lack of evidence with evidence of failure, and discarding everything the campaign had learned every time they restart.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Every Advertising Decision Is Actually an Inventory Decision
resources.summary: The most expensive PPC mistake isn't overspending on ads — it's creating demand your supply chain can't support. Advertising doesn't report demand, it writes purchase orders your supplier hasn't seen yet.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Inventory Forecasting Is Not a Math Problem
resources.summary: Sellers who keep stocking out rarely have a formula problem — they have a decision problem. Why extra precision in the arithmetic doesn't fix a constraint that lives in cash, lead time and asymmetric risk.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: How AI and Customer Interviews Predict Market Demand
resources.summary: Forecasting demand before the data exists — what models can infer from weak signals, what only a conversation with a real buyer reveals, and why the two together beat either alone.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: You're Measuring the Wrong KPI: Why Great Amazon Businesses Stop Chasing Advertising Metrics
resources.summary: The biggest mistake experienced sellers make isn't choosing the wrong KPI — it's asking the wrong question. Advertising dashboards describe yesterday; businesses must decide tomorrow.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Your PPC Campaigns Are Probably Stealing Sales From Each Other
resources.summary: The competition hurting your advertising performance may not be your competitors. Amazon reports each campaign individually — it almost never tells you how they interact.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Advertising Debt: The Hidden Liability Almost Every Amazon Business Is Building
resources.summary: The most dangerous dependency in your business doesn't appear on your balance sheet. It's the gap between the sales you generate today and the sales you'd generate if advertising stopped tomorrow.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The Most Important PPC Question Isn't “Did It Generate Sales?” It's “Would Those Sales Have Happened Anyway?”
resources.summary: Attribution tells you where a sale was recorded. Incrementality tells you where value was created. Spend $100K, see $620K attributed — how much of it would have arrived anyway?
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Stop Managing Campaigns. Start Managing an Advertising Portfolio.
resources.summary: The best Amazon advertisers don't think like marketers — they think like investment managers. Your account isn't a collection of campaigns. It's a portfolio, and portfolios are managed differently.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Your Highest ROAS Campaign May Be Holding Your Business Back
resources.summary: The campaigns that look best on your dashboard are not always the ones creating the most value. ROAS measures attributed sales — not whether those sales were incremental.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Your PPC Campaigns Aren't Competing Against Your Competitors. They're Competing Against Each Other.
resources.summary: The biggest battle in your advertising account isn't in Amazon's auction. It's inside your own business — campaigns competing for inventory, capital, supplier capacity and attention.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: PPC Is Not a Marketing Problem. It's a Capital Allocation Problem.
resources.summary: The biggest advertising decisions aren't made inside Campaign Manager. They're made when you decide where the next dollar goes — and advertising competes with every other investment in the business.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Stop Optimizing ACOS: Why Chasing a Lower ACOS Is Costing You More Money
resources.summary: The most dangerous number in Amazon advertising isn't a high ACOS — it's believing ACOS should always go down. Why an efficiency metric makes a poor decision metric.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Your Inventory Isn't Costing You Storage Fees. It's Costing You Optionality.
resources.summary: The most expensive inventory in your warehouse isn't the one paying long-term storage fees. It's the one preventing your next opportunity.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The Opportunity Cost Every Amazon Seller Ignores
resources.summary: Ask a seller what a purchase order costs and they'll quote the invoice. The real cost is every alternative that order made impossible — and it never appears on a P&L.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Your Best-Selling Product Might Be Your Worst Investment
resources.summary: Why the SKU generating the most revenue isn't always the one that deserves your next dollar. Revenue measures popularity, not efficiency — and every purchase order is really an investment decision.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: The Metric That Matters More Than Profit (And Almost No Amazon Seller Tracks It)
resources.summary: Two sellers, same revenue, same margin, same profit — and five years later they're not the same size. Profit tells you how much you earned. Capital velocity tells you how many chances your money had to earn it.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Inventory Forecasting Isn't About Finding the Perfect Formula — It's About Asking Better Questions
resources.summary: One expert says use the simple reorder formula. Another says it's fundamentally flawed. Both are right. The real mistake is treating forecasting as a maths problem when it's a decision-making one.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Why the Classic Amazon Reorder Formula Is Wrong (For Most Sellers)
resources.summary: It isn't wrong because the maths is incorrect — it's wrong because its assumptions rarely match how Amazon businesses operate. Seven problems with the standard reorder point, and a better alternative for each.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Amazon Inventory Reorder Point: The Simple Formula Every Seller Should Know
resources.summary: Most stockouts begin weeks before you run out — at the moment you miss placing the next order. The reorder point formula, the five metrics to check weekly, and the warning signs to never ignore.
resources.author: AmazeBase

resources.title: Inventory Forecasting: The Mistakes That Quietly Destroy Your Profit
resources.summary: Order too little and you lose sales, rankings and momentum. Order too much and your cash sits in a warehouse. The ten mistakes that cause both — and what to do instead.
resources.author: AmazeBase
